problem_clarity.rationale: The problem is concrete and specific: free online projectile calculators assume a flat Earth, Earth gravity (~9.81 m/s^2), and drag, all invalid on the Moon (~1.62 m/s^2, ~1737 km radius, no atmosphere), and at mass-driver velocities lunar curvature dominates so flat parabolic formulas are materially wrong; meanwhile professional suites (GMAT, STK) are heavyweight, desktop-licensed, and overkill. The proposal identifies an empty niche for a fast in-browser 3D lunar mass-driver tool and names the underserved users (students, educators, concept designers).

scope_boundedness.rationale: The MVP is bounded: a single-page client-side app with explicit inputs (launch position, muzzle velocity, azimuth, elevation), explicit outputs (impact coords, great-circle range, flight time, apogee, peak speed), three core modules (physics solver, 3D renderer, UI), and a clear out-of-scope list (multi-body, mascons, terrain DEMs, warhead/effects, backend, saved scenarios). However the proposal itself states that the chosen physics fidelity (parabola vs. Keplerian) and the delivery-vs-strike intent materially change what should be built, so the exact scope is contingent on two unresolved answers.

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Seven stakeholder/actor types are enumerated with a primary/secondary split (mission-design students, educators, indie sim devs, space-enthusiast makers, plus an unidentified product owner/sponsor, an unidentified physics validator, and a conditional policy/export-control reviewer). But the most important actor — a confirmed sponsor or real customer — is explicitly unidentified; the proposal states no sponsor artifacts exist and that the existence of a real user base is an unconfirmed assumption.

assumption_visibility.rationale: Six explicit, clearly labeled assumptions are stated (point mass with no thrust/lift/drag, no atmosphere, central inverse-square gravity, instantaneous muzzle velocity at fixed elevation/azimuth, static surface target, client-side no backend, and a benign-tool framing pending intent clarification). They are visible, explicit, and testable.

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Six unknowns are well-articulated (intent, physics fidelity, rotation/mascons, performance target, sponsor existence, export-control treatment) and most are resolvable through clarification or standard engineering work. However two — delivery-vs-strike intent and the parabola-vs-Keplerian fidelity target — are flagged as material and currently unresolved, which is precisely why the proposal recommends 'clarify' rather than 'go'.

risk_visibility.rationale: Five categorized risks are listed with severity ratings: regulatory/ethical (high, conditional on the strike interpretation), domain accuracy (high), positioning (medium), technical (medium), and sponsorship/sustainability (medium). The dominant risks are visible and each is tied to a specific unknown.

evidence_grounding.rationale: Evidence is honest but thin, as expected for greenfield: artifact_list returns 0 artifacts and repository_checkout_list returns 0 checkouts (confirming the absence of any prior spec or product code), and the bound repo is the Saga tooling host rather than a product implementation. Physical constants are explicitly labeled general domain knowledge rather than fabricated citations. However the central problem claim — that the in-browser 3D lunar mass-driver niche is empty — rests on general domain knowledge with no competitive/market scan, and no sponsor/customer evidence exists.

blocking_gaps.description: The source phrase 'доставки/поражения' supports both benign logistics delivery and weaponized strike; this is unresolved and materially reshapes ethics, features, and regulatory/export-control (ITAR/EAR, Outer Space Treaty) posture. A clean go/reject settlement cannot be made until a sponsor clarifies the intended use.

The required solver fidelity — flat-surface parabola vs. central-gravity/Keplerian — is unresolved and sets core solver complexity, the toy-vs-tool positioning, and ultimately what should be built; the proposal cannot be turned into an actionable build spec without this answer.

non_blocking_gaps.description: No confirmed sponsor or customer artifacts exist; primary users are plausible but assumed. Non-blocking for an MVP-sized client-side build but must be confirmed before any sustainability/adoption claim can be trusted.

The central claim that no fast in-browser 3D lunar mass-driver tool exists (the empty niche) rests on general aerospace domain knowledge with no competitive scan or market evidence; should be validated before the niche is treated as established.

Performance targets (trajectories per second, max simultaneous projectiles, minimum supported device class) are unspecified, leaving the non-functional requirements underscoped relative to the stated technical/performance risk.

payload.rationale: The proposal is internally coherent, well-structured, and honest about its assumptions, unknowns, and risks, so it is well-formed enough to be assessed. But it is not unconditionally ready for settlement: two material clarifications (delivery-vs-strike intent and parabola-vs-Keplerian fidelity) genuinely change what should be built and cannot be assumed away reversibly; the sponsor is unconfirmed; and the empty-niche claim lacks competitive evidence. This aligns with the proposal's own recommended_outcome of 'clarify'; the appropriate next action is to request clarification rather than proceed to settlement.
